title: F-droid Version 1.61.105-t7429e8912-g12210d3f26b crashes at launch
body:
### What is the issue?

The tailscale android  app crashes immediately upon launching on both my nvidia shield and pixel phone. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Tailscale F-droid version 1.61.105-t7429e8912-g12210d3f26b
2. Attempt to open the app.

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

_No response_

_No response_

Android 14

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I understand & acknowledge that errors, in any way, can & will happen, so I don’t want to blame anyone with my comment. But in my opinion, this issue is critical & should deserve more immediate actions:

- on F-Droid, select the former, working version as suggested immediately, to prevent more users from running into this issue
- rebuild the last working version (`1.58.2-tb0e1bbb62-gcd1f0649958`) and push it to F-Droid as version something like `1.61.106-really1.58.2`

I think those immediate actions are reasonable because this issue breaks Tailscale for all users using F-Droid & it is hard to revert that issue:
- Android, I think starting with version 13, has an app downgrade protection enabled. So it prevents users from just downgrading the app.
- Because the app [prevents being part of system backups](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android/blob/a1d97baeb02948b842645394dcd8a3b81132e9d1/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L29), I also cannot just remove the app & install a former version and then am good to go. Rather, I need to:
  - reauthenticate in the app
  - the app gets a new IPv4 assigned (admins may change that to the old one)
  - because the "old app" was not properly signed out, it still blocks the MagicDNS hostname, so I get there a new one as well (admins can fix that)
  - if Tailscale Lock is enabled, the app needs to be resigned



> Ideally F-Droid would pause for a bit until the new app is ready. It won't be long.

@participant2 can you maybe estimate more exactly when the new app release will happen? I cannot really determine if you mean something like 1-2 days or 1-2 weeks. (in case pushing the latest working version is not possible)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant4, we at Tailscale are not involved in the F-Droid packaging or release decisions. We put code on GitHub and other people put it on F-Droid.

Our version numbering scheme is minor numbers that are even are stable (58) and odd are unstable dev releases (like 61). Apparently somebody put a random snapshot of in-progress code on F-Droid (61 is odd) that we never released or tested ourselves and it crashes. That's not code we would ship (and didn't ship to the Google Play Store).

So, yes, F-Droid should probably roll back to a stable release that worked. But that's not in my power.

I won't speak for the Android team on their schedule. But it seems to be moving very rapidly so I don't think it'll take two weeks. F-Droid should probably be ready to package it within a week.

> Which tag was F-Droid built against?

As visible [in this file](https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/blob/10dd6efbd96609326b5a4e19e2e1405eb6f3c0d3/metadata/com.tailscale.ipn.yml), IIUC:
- version `1.61.105-t7429e8912-g12210d3f26b`, the one which was released, was built against tag [1.63.93-t1fbaf2610-ge0020f8c4bf](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android/releases/tag/1.63.93-t1fbaf2610-ge0020f8c4bf) but using the subdir `android_legacy` ([src](https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/blob/10dd6efbd96609326b5a4e19e2e1405eb6f3c0d3/metadata/com.tailscale.ipn.yml#L1293-1297))
- version `1.64.0-t78dc8622d-gfd2ca6fa940` (not yet released, but tested by participant3) was build against commit [97cc00210ee30d4f1ca5cbe67bb7642b31629de4](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android/commit/97cc00210ee30d4f1ca5cbe67bb7642b31629de4) also using the subdir `android_legacy` ([src](https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/blob/10dd6efbd96609326b5a4e19e2e1405eb6f3c0d3/metadata/com.tailscale.ipn.yml#L1329-1333))

I assume esp. for the first, the F-Droid bot was triggered by the tag (which I assume was meant for the new app stored in `/android`?) but then built from the dir `/android_legacy.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
> I have disabled the crashed versions. But the users have to reinstall the old versions manually since Android doesn't allow downgrading.

@participant3 Can I confirm that the workaround is:

1. There's no possibility of a direct-downgrade via F-Droid.
2. The app must be uninstalled, then when we attempt to reinstall, the suggested version will be `1.58.2-tb0e1bbb62-gcd1f0649958` published on 2/10/24 (or eventually something newer that isn't broken) will be the suggested version?
3. We should expect to deal manually deal with the fallout of the issues described by @participant4 related to having to re-register the tailscale client and get a new identity/ip?

Edit: And I suppose another follow-up is that having disabled the new/broken versions... there's nothing else you plan to or really can do until the next newer version that works comes out... next-week-ish. And that if folks do wait it out, the upgrade should "just work" without re-registration... the obvious downside being an extended downtime on the device while waiting for the upgrade?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
For anyone watching here for status...

`1.60.1-t2caffeeb4-g6f7ae79a31c` released to fdroid yesterday on 4/17 addresses the issue for me and Tailscale no longer crashes on startup. If you waited the issue out and did NOT uninstall, the client "just" connects as normal. If you uninstalled, then presumably you had to re-register your client.

comments.author: participant8

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
@participant3 @participant7 note that [1.66.3 has been tagged](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android/releases/tag/1.66.3-teae73f821-g63a2bbc8e71) on the tailscale-android repo. You can release that tag to F-Droid users if you wish.

In general, at any given time, the latest commit tagged with an even minor version number is always safe to release to users (1.62.1, 1.64.0, 1.66.3), etc. Any release with an odd minor version number should be ignored.
